method: Whole header read and specified implementation ranges only; source bytes checked against stored pinned Git tree.
findings: Buffer allocation acquires count semaphore before allocating; free releases it. Limit counts buffers, not a direct process-wide byte cap. Paranoid mode bypasses this semaphore.

RmBuffer stores allocation size and filled length as guint32 whereas allocation API accepts gsize; no input-range enforcement is shown in inspected allocation function. Large-size runtime behavior not tested.
Paranoid equality falls back to shadow digest equality when first operand buffers are absent; strict byte-proof conclusions therefore require lifecycle analysis of buffer release and callers.
With buffers present, ordinary slow path compares each block length/content and requires simultaneous list exhaustion; pre-matched twin/reject shortcuts precede it.
Header explicitly defines cumulative digest as order-insensitive. Such a digest cannot by itself prove ordered file-byte identity.
limits: lib/checksum.c is only partially read and receives no whole-file credit.
No runtime tests or production changes in this increment; caller lifecycle and complete checksum implementation remain to inspect.
Native pHash deferred; global full repository count remains150/500.
